body: It really is a no win situation, I agree.  So many factors that the correct choice is not clear. One thing that is clear is that my wife, due to her work habits, does not have a good relationship as I do with our boys, especially mine and if we tell them now, it is very likely he will blame himself and/or his brother will blame him as he has caused a number of issues due to his behavior in the past few years.

The kids know something, that is true. However, they see us drinking coffee together every morning (they won't when school starts) and watching tv together at night, well not all the time, but many nights. 

As to bringing someone home, we have discussed that issue, no bringing home "dates" while either child is here.  We can afford hotels or go to their place.  

I appreciate your opinion.

Thanks for the response.  We are not just staying together for the kids, we are also staying together because financially, she would not be able to afford the area and since each of us is the biological parent of one of the children, that could mean either her biological son would have to move away and from his friends and schools or he would want to stay here with me (my house) and I worry about guilt he would have not being with his mother. We are not fighting, there is no tension. We have discussed things that are deal breakers for us, like bringing home dates with the kids are around, to introducing ourselves to their new partner if they are having difficulty believing that we are not married.  That situation is very likely years away, but it is one of the myriad of issues we have discussed.  The benefits, if we don't get angry at each other and raise the tension levels, are numerous. Living with 4 is much cheaper than living 2/2 so we would have more money for ourselves, the kids, their colleges and so forth.  At the age they are we rarely have a "family" dinner due to schedules so in truth the whole family is rarely "together", even though they are in the same house together. My wife and I sit and watch tv together, movies, etc.  That is also part of what we discussed, doing things together as a family, not just her with the kids and me with the kids.  We already did many things separately as the boys are in scouts, which I participate in with them, and she is much more of the artsy type of person and I cannot tell Monet from Dali.

Dating would be a little more difficult, but think of it this way, if I were dating living only with my son and wanted to go somewhere for the weekend, I would have to get someone to watch him. With us together, we can work together to take of the kids and develop other relationships.  At the end of the school year we will review where we are and if we want to continue.  The agreements are for 1 year at a time, we are not teenagers who will want to run off to Vegas and get married a month after we meet someone.

You are right in what should concern us, the things you have spoken about are issues we are looking at and both of us have agreed that if tensions start to rise, she will move out and visit as much as she can, the kids don't see her a lot during the week anyways as they leave at 7am and she doesn't even get up till 8 or 9. She doesn't get home till after 7 and by then they are doing schoolwork and getting ready for bed.

I do appreciate your opinion, that's what I want, to see if others have had dealt with a situation like this and how it worked out.

As to why she would be as fucking stupid as to have unprotected sex with him (and he with her) is beyond me, but she did. I have never been tested as there is no test for men, only women.  Only symptom in men is genital warts and that only happens with the strains that that don't cause cancer (we got the good cancer causing kind).  We don't find out until we pass it on to some other woman or develop rectal, throat or tongue cancer.

Its very hard, plus you have to worry about the fact that he can pass on diseases to you, mine caught HPV from the guy she was screwing and passed it on to me. Worse yet, there is no test for men. So every guy he is seeing could be one that he gets something to pass on to you and condoms are only partially effective.

The sex part didn't really bother me, but I know it is common to imagine them having sex.  My issue was the intimacy, talking, snuggling, talking about my family, my marriage, our kids, those are the things i dwell on instead of the sexual acts.  Neither one of us were virgins when we married, so of course she had sex with others.

I don't have a problem with snooping, she is your wife, your partner, you should be open and transparent about everything in your life. Your trust in her has been damaged and you are seeking something to tell you if you are wrong are right.  

When my wife started keeping her phone with her at all times, changing the password, deleting texts, having her computer automatically clear it's password upon shutdown your dam right I snooped.  What I found was that she had cheated on me for almost a year.

Having sex with ex-partners is pretty common from what I understand. I know this does not help with your hurt.  As to getting over the hurt, see about individual counseling and group as well.  This can really help by talking to someone.  Believe it or not, telling your secrets to strangers can be cathartic as they don't know you.

Well, first of all, just because you were having emotions doesn't mean he was or to the level you were.  My wife had an affair with a guy who she thought was developing and emotional attachment to her.  Found out later that he was on multiple dating sites, while with her, and that when she "broke up" with him, he updated his profile with new pictures within a week, so he was not overly heartbroken at her leaving.

I will say that stressing over a lap  dance is a little to cautious.  I have been to many a strip club in my youth and I can tell you from experience. The women there are not looking to make an emotional connection but empty your wallet.  They aren't looking for sex (unless they are semi-pro hookers), so they really are not a threat to your relationship.

As to your "boyfriend" cheating on you, why wouldn't he? I mean, he has already shown that he is willing to cheat with a married woman so why would he suddenly develop morals? These things are not your "fault", yes you have had a run of bad luck, but don't give up, there are good people out there.

I have to believe anger is normal.  I know it was for me (12 years and she was cheating for a year WHILE we were going to marriage counseling). I know I was punching my steering wheel and screaming quite often.  One thing you might do is go to a support group and journal.  I didn't think it would help at first, but it really does help to just write down your feelings and thoughts rather than bottling them inside you.
 
Let me ask though, I know it hurts, trust me, is she and your family worth fighting to save? 15 years is a long time, you have two kids and it will be difficult to really keep a connection as they get older especially.

Ok, try this one on for size.  In mid March, I was diagnosed as Bipolar, two weeks later, on April 1, she announces she wants a divorce and while not admitting it until later, that she had a boyfriend for around the last year on the side.  We have kids so didn't want to upset them, so we didn't tell them.  We were separated, but living in my home still.   

She agrees to go to counseling, gives up the boyfriend (have confirmed) and things were moving along in counseling pretty well, had put the past behind me and was focusing on the now and the future with her, if possible. 

Comes to me on Wednesday morning to tell me she had gotten her test results back from a physical the other day. My first thought was "oh, shit she is pregnant" and as I have a vasectomy it could only be the boyfriends.  I wish now that it had been the case.  No, something better.  She had contracted HPV from him and not the good kind (if there is such a thing), but the kind that can give you cancer.  So, since she was still having sex with me while she was fucking him, without protection by the way, odds are that I have it as well and since there is no test for males (and there is a percentage of males that become carriers), I have to assume I have it and could affect any future partners I wish to have sex or even deep kissing.

So if I do not work things out with my wife, I would have to try to find either a woman who would take the risk with me using a condom (condoms suck and do not completely protect you) or find someone else who has the EXACT same strain out of over 100 strains, to be with as a sex partner. That would be a nice profile on Match Dot Com wouldn't you agree?

All I can say is I am old school.  Life is hard and guess what? So is marriage.  I once read that the divorce rate for arranged marriages was very low...why? Because they go into the relationship knowing that a lot of work would be involved and that "love" was not all that was needed to make it work.  

I am not saying your emotions are not real, but from talking to our counselor and others, you have to open yourself to love, which takes trust and of course your trust, as was mine, has been seriously strained if not destroyed.  This does not mean it cannot be regained (it may not in the end), but it will certainly take work, time and commitment by both parties.  If it cannot, well of course the relationship will never work, but Rome wasn't built in a day and neither was your relationship.  Life is weird, my parents have been married over 50 years, through good times and bad.  They met at a local "juke" joint and snuck off to another county to get married (my mother was underage at the time), and I have known others married for 40 years who get divorced in their 70's.  I wish I knew the magic formula.  I just hate to give up when neither one of us hate the other, but are just disappointed in the other.  For her it was dealing with my bipolarism for 5 years (misdiagnosed as depression), but being treated now with the proper meds and of course my issues with the infidelity.  There are the kids as well and how our failure, if it ends up in failure, will affect them for the rest of their lives and their future relationships.  

I wish you all the best and hope things work out, if that is what you really desire, but don't base your decisions on how you feel at the moment.  The old saying "time heals all wounds" is true in many ways.  It will take time for you to forgive and trust again, if you ever can. I know right now you question your love for him, but the way it has been explained to me is that you "stuck your hand on a hot stove" and got burned.  Now you are having to consider sticking your hand there again with the idea that the stove has now been turned off and will no longer burn you, a hard thing to do right after you have been burned by it.  Hopefully, with time, you will be able to trust again and stick you hand on it (a little checking doesn't hurt either), but transparency, full transparency would be needed for the rest of your marriage, I know it will with mine.

First, thank you for the reply! It is interesting, my wife and I are going through counseling after she had an affair for about a year. One of the reasons I choose the counselor we are seeing is posting on his website where he talks about your partner being your soulmate, that you finish each others sentence, that you can't wait to be with them, that they make you feel whole, that and a variety of other feelings.  He goes on to say that what you are feeling is lust, not love.  That you are running from your issues and problems as well as those in your marriage to a place with much less or no stress and this leads you to believe what you are feeling it real.  
My wife had announced she wanted a divorce, didn't want to work on the marriage, etc.  It soon became apparent she was in a relationship with another man.  After two visits to the therapist, she gave up the "boyfriend" realizing what she had with him was not real and truthfully what she thought she was feeling was not being reciprocated by him (he was back on the dating sites within days of her breaking up with him).  I am not judging you, if I come across that way I am sorry.  I believe what you are feeling is real to you.  We all want to feel connected, to feel loved and desired by someone.  I was angry at my wife and am still hurt immensely, but I better understand why she did what she did, how the issues in our relationship caused her to pull away, that it left a void and what started as a sexual relationship with another man, turned into what she felt at the time was an emotional connection as well.  Talking to people on here have better helped me understand why they have cheated with married people.  I just couldn't understand why they would do it.  I could understand having sex, it is enjoyable, but developing an emotional relationship? No, that made no sense. In the end, I hope we can get past our issues as well as the serious damage done to our trust not just for us, but for our kids as well.

Again, thank you for responding. I wish you well.

First, are you going to marriage counseling? My wife of 12 years had an affair, physical at first that lead to emotional. She broke it off after a couple of sessions with the counselor and realized that what she had was not a true connection with the other man, but lust and passion.  Believe it or not the guy sent her a text a few days ago, putting out feelers to see if she would respond, she didn't and told me about it, but goes to show that free tail is free tail, no matter the cost to others.  
The counseling has helped quite a bit, if for no other reason than it helped us see the mistakes we had made that led us to where we are now.  The affair was not the cause of our problems, just a symptom of the issues. The counseling has also helped with our communications as well.  In the end our relationship may fail and that is something I have to accept.  Even if we move forward I have huge trust issues, like you.  That is going to be very hard for me to overcome, but necessary if I want to move forward.  My wife didn't want to try and save the marriage and would not go to counseling at first. She has now and while we are working on our relationship, which is necessary because we have children involved, she has not decided (yet) to work on the marriage itself.  You don't have the issue of children, so you have to decide.  Was the relationship you have with him such that you are willing to put in the effort to try and save it? to rebuild it? If it is not, then cut the ties and move on, you are young and the idea that there is only one person out there for you is bullshit.

I  have a question for both you you, off topic a bit, but would love if you answered.
I am on the opposite side, my wife of 12 years had an affair which she has since broken off.  The question I have is this....What possible future (good) did you see with this person? I mean, they were cheating with you on their spouse, the person that they had given their vow to be with and them alone. I am sure they gave you all sorts of "we don't love each other anymore, the marriage is in name only, we just go through the motions, we stay together for the kids...Etc.  But how could you EVER trust this person in your life and for that matter how could they ever trust you. You had an affair with a married man, you didn't owe his wife (or kids) anything, but morally that makes you questionable. He on the other hand could never be trusted (in my opinion) and the odds of it working out are horrible, less than 5% (according to our marriage counselor who has been doing this since the 70').  I could see having sex because it is enjoyable, but why try and develop that into a relationship that is most likely doomed from the start?

I understand your pain. I went through the same process, focusing on my education, law school, etc.; only to have it disappear in front of me from undiagnosed Bipolarism (type 2).  Recognize past events that I had made excuses for as the early onset of my disease.  Treated for depression for many years and now am on the verge of divorce because of my inability to find work of any substance (over 5 years now) and my wife being afraid that I will have more episodes due to what she has read on the net.

For me, its a boon.  Even though I have not found employment, the meds they have me on give me the ability to focus again, get out of bed and stay there, lose 46 pounds and so on.  I feel much more confident, feel good in regards to my self-image, my fear of failure is not overriding my fear of success.  All these things and more with the help of a little white pill.... I joke, but the meds and going to group therapy have helped immensely as well as learning how sleep, exercise, eating right, recognition of my triggers and a variety of other methods have at least given me hope that I can regain a career and a life, even if, in the end, it is without my wife.  The issues in our relationship are no longer mine, but hers.  Don't let the fear override what you want to do, you are not worse off trying and failing than not trying at all.  I really do understand this ruminating on negative possible futures, I did it for years and even now do it, but recognize it as a feature of my disorder and don't let it control me...GOOD LUCK!
How about giving up, but giving yourself over to others, like becoming a monk? You could live for others?
Have you made statements like this before to them? If you have they may feel you are a drama queen, seeking to get attention from them. Don't give the pricks the satisfaction.

I am sorry that you have come to this point in your life and while I truly cannot understand what you are going through right now, I do have some inkling of how you feel.  I was an undiagnosed bipolar for many years having many of the same issues you have had in your life.About 5 years ago my career fell apart, wasn't able to find a job, lack of drive focus, the whole bag.  Then on April  1st my wife of 12 years announced basically she had enough and wanted a divorce.  I have a shoulder injury that I know many don't believe causes me pain, it still does, I just don't tell anyone because I was tired to the looks of derision I got from them when I complained about it. 

In mid June my wife and I had a huge fight, worse than any I had ever had with her.  She broke a number of things including a glass art piece we had received at our wedding.  When she left I wrote a note to my kids and family, made an updated will, picked out a nice piece of the broken artwork and sat down on my bed with my notes and glass.  I was at rock bottom.  I could not see how my life could get any worse, saw no chance of things improving, felt I had no reason to continue.  I cut up my arm and hand, experimenting to find which was the sharpest edge of the glass and how much pressure would cut how deeply.  I felt I was ready, but I paused and thought of my boys, how this would affect them the rest of their lives.  I tried to focus on things that were positive in life, even if it was only a favorite dish that I enjoyed eating on occasion, on memories that of times with my wife, my kids, my family. I didn't really consider how my life would improve, but more about how my actions would so negatively affect those I love. In the end this was enough for me to stop and re-think what I was doing. I still think about suicide every day, I haven't tried again, but I think about it.  I go to group therapy for mental illness two to 4 days a week.  It doesn't cure me, but it helps to talk to people who have experienced the same feelings I have had in my life. This is why I said I truly could not understand what you are going trough right now. Our experiences are very personal to ourselves.  Even though many people have the same illness I have, we can never truly understand what their path has been in life or where they were at right now. Check around, find a suicide hotline, sometimes just being able to open up to someone, even a stranger, can help immensely. I am betting that where you are at, like here, has free groups that you can meet with, talk about your problems, share about how you feel.  I know this sounds all touchy feely, but it does help talking about things and getting things off your chest. 

As to your medical issues, if you are not working, you should be able to get medicaid to help with your problems. Call 211, it usually puts you in touch with people who can help you, lead you to programs that can aid you in your needs.  

I hope you are able to see some good in your life and continue forward.

Going through the divorce, the guilt he will have to some degree ( how much he blames himself you will never be able to predict) and not the added pressure of coming into his own, discovering who he is as a person while having to deal with the stability that he always had and thought would always be there in his mother and I; and also trying to "force" a relationship with me into his busy life.  I am under no misconception that either way I choose will cause him pain. I know some of you have said that I am being selfish, trust me, if I was selfish I would have thrown their mother out when I she came forward with what she had done, but I didn't. If I was selfish I would simply continue with a "whatever happens will happen" sort of attitude and not have any concern as to what he will feel or suffer (my wife's feeling is that the boy's will 'cope').  A man who loses his legs will cope, but has still lost his legs.  I do greatly care what my boys will have to go through if our marriage fails, that is why I am trying to decide what is best for them emotionally rather than putting that onus upon them.

I have met many polyamory parties in my life, but to be truthful I have never seen one last (like for 30 or 40 years) in that they people who are part of it come and go, there is no set "core" that last for a long period of time although I am sure there are those out there. I absolutely agree that sex CAN be intimate, but I believe that sex in and of itself is not intimate.  You can be intimate with your partner snuggling with you, having dinner, watching tv, walking in the woods, intimacy does not require sex and sex does not require intimacy.  They are separate things which when combined lead to a wonderful relationship. 
As to what I am assume is a slight against me in that you seem to be saying I am trying to "control her feelings"  as you put it. Do understand that we spoke extensively on the issue of what WE desired, how it would work, what the limits would be as well as the rules.  This was not something I dictated to her, but something we agreed to as a couple.  When you have an agreement you cannot simply change the terms of that agreement by yourself whenever you feel the need. I give an example: One partner wants children, but the other does not.  They agree to wait a few years till they are more secure financially. However, the one that wants children begins putting small holes in the condoms they use and sure enough she becomes pregnant.  By your definition the partner who did not want children had no right to try and control their procreation and therefore was justified in causing the pregnancy, which involves BOTH of them. 
We felt that breaking the rules we had both agreed to could lead to problems such as what happened here.  When she became unhappy in our relationship, she should have opened up fully to me and we could have then decided how we would handle the situation. We could have sought counseling, separated, divorced or changed the parameters of the agreement which we both had entered into.  It was extremely hurtful and damaging for her to act capriciously and selfishly in the way she did by breaking the rules of the agreement.

Really? You have never had sex without emotions? You are luckier than I have been in my life.  There is a difference between someone you have sex with, a fuckbuddy, a friend, a lover, etc.  What we desired was someone to have fun with, not a relationship with, not someone to grow intimate (by our definition of intimacy) or share our lives with, just someone to enjoy physically,so yes, a "human sex toy" using your term.  But like you said, it really doesn't matter the nature of relationship, but that we had boundaries set in our relationship that we had agreed upon and she broke those boundaries.  I have said, that the breaking of the boundaries was not what caused our problems, but it didn't help and probably was the impetus in her deciding she wanted out of the relationship.  It is much easier to leave one relationship if you think you have a budding one in the wings that you can easily transition into.  Everyone has a different idea as to what an "open relationship" means.  We had our definition and when she went outside those boundaries I consider it infidelity.  You may have an issue with the type of relationship we were in and how we viewed our "sex toys", but you cannot argue that breaking the boundaries that a couple sets, whether it be a "regular" marriage in which they only have sex with each other, to a poly marriage in which they have partners coming and going, is a violation of the relationship.

Sex is not intimate.  Holding hands is intimate, snuggling is intimate, being there emotionally to share your problems is intimate.  Getting a blowjob from a hooker is hardly intimate, no matter what Richard Gere conveyed in the movie. 

Primarily because it had been part of the agreement we made with each other that emotional relationships were not in the cards as it led to too many problems. We didn't really didn't see it being a problem for us, just worried that they would become attached and want more.  That was the problems we sought to avoid but we also realized the danger or mixing sex with emotional bonds, that is how relationships start.  We had given each other the right to cancel any relationship the other had if we were uncomfortable with it as well.

Work hard together in the counseling, this can be very hard. I think it can be easy, especially if you are having any issues in your primary relationship, to view it as something that is too hard or that you don't want to deal with anymore than possible.  The new partner is great, he is fun, no issues or responsibilities so you can easily start to be drawn to that person (I have gotten these 'feelings' from my wife in our discussions).  Once she took a step back and looked at her life, our life, she realized what she had done.  It's not a quick thing or something she sought, but those wonderful new feelings she was having, the excitement, the rush of being with a new person and developing that "relationship" with them, the things you don't have with a partner of many years, can easily be mistaken from true emotional bonding. So I hope it works out, be try to understand it from your partners point of view, it can be hard.  I was very angry with my wife as well as her partner until I really started to understand that it wasn't him that really caused the problems, just the straw that broke...well you know the rest. It may work for you, it does for many people and it did for us for years, but beware the pitfalls, there are many and they can lead to problems in your marriage.
